body.target_estimand: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) is the endpoint-invariance structural target over the note's finite-alphabet faithful shared-response compatibility fiber. On the separate fixed-\(A\) purely graphical fiber, the established result is \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e)=\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)\). At law level, \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{faith}}(e)\subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e)\); singleton \(\mathcal G_A\) gives equality automatically, whereas two-mark equality requires nonempty faithful realization fibers. Equality of a fixed observable rule closure with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) remains a conditional implication requiring faithful realization and an unknown-\(A\) extension theorem.
body.estimand_functional: For \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\) if and only if \(\mu_\eta(e)=m\) for every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\) otherwise, where \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) is formed inside the finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) defined in this note, not the entire published graphical class.

sampling_model.design: Oracle graphical analysis uses the observational selected-law MAG signature and \(K\) pooled binary-indicator MAG signatures coupled by one model-specific basal selected DAG. The structural target is endpoint invariance over the note's finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass; the established results are exact on a separate fixed-\(A\) graphical fiber and conditional at the unknown-\(A\) law level.
sampling_model.units: The primitive law-level object is \(\eta=(S_\eta,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},(\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K})\), generated by one shared-exogenous response-function family. At \(K=0\), its oracle law is \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S_\eta^*=\mathbf1)\); for each \(k\in[K]\), the comparison uses the pooled law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Regime membership is observed. Each direct soft-intervention target set \(T_k(\eta)\) is latent and may differ from the indicator-neighbor set \(Z_k\), which can also contain indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables.
sampling_model.overlap: The common basal selection event \(S_\eta^*=\mathbf1\) has positive probability for every law-level model, so all selected and pooled oracle laws are defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not applicable to the proved oracle statements. No finite-sample conditional-independence or invariance tests, separation margin, or simultaneous error-control theorem is assumed or established.

body.tldr: Selection before perturbation couples all pooled regime MAGs through one basal selected DAG. The note now proves the exact fixed-\(A\) endpoint mark set on a purely graphical Dai fiber and separates it from the law-level faithful bracket: singleton graphical mark sets identify the faithful endpoint automatically, while opposing faithful witnesses in the two-mark case still require nonempty realization fibers. A supplied nonempty open rational shared-response parameterization yields a finite exceptional-set argument only after atomic determinant nontriviality is certified. The parameterization construction, those atomic certificates, the finite observable unknown-\(A\) rule list, canonical endpoint equality, and simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs remain open.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. prove CDIS soundness and leave completeness uncertain; their graphical endpoint semantics do not supply opposing faithful representatives from one shared-response twin SCM. Zhang proves completeness for one observational PAG, not synchronized pooled intervention MAGs with unknown targets and pre-treatment selection. The exact remaining law-level gap is twofold: construct a nonempty open equality-constrained shared-response parameterization for every replacement specification and prove atomic determinant nontriviality on it. Even an affirmative realization theorem would still leave the finite observable unknown-\(A\) common-exterior extension problem.
project_justification.niche: The achieved contribution is an exact structural characterization on the fixed-\(A\) purely graphical fiber, together with a sharply separated faithful-model bracket and conditional endpoint-equality theorem. It is a technical foundation below a complete-calculus result, not a field-level completeness or inference theorem.
project_justification.fill: The note exposes three distinct maps. It computes \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\) by explicit empty-graph and simple signature-monotone-path constructions; it embeds the nonempty faithful mark set inside that graphical set, obtaining automatic equality only in singleton cases; and it proves that faithful realization plus a fixed observable unknown-\(A\) extension property would imply equality of a candidate rule closure with the canonical SI-PAG. Conditional saturation needs at most \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates. Neither open antecedent is silently inferred from graphical inclusion.

body.related_work: Dai et al.'s Lemmas 3--6 provide the graphical twin-MAG interface for causally sufficient, childless pre-treatment selection, while their Theorem 3 establishes CDIS soundness and their discussion leaves completeness uncertain. The present note uses a finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass of those graphical models and does not claim equality with Dai et al.'s full law class. Zhang's Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for a single observational PAG, but not simultaneous common-basal pooled regimes. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes provide single-MAG equivalence invariants that motivate full-signature preservation, not faithful common-basal realization. The public Zhou--Kocaoglu abstract concerns known-target completion with enumeration, which is excluded here as a headline calculus. Wang, Du, and Zhou inform computational context; the present computable statement is only the conditional bound of \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict endpoint updates for a supplied fixed rule list. Jaber et al. treat unknown targets without selection, and Luo et al. concern a distinct post-treatment-selection setting. Relative to these comparators, the result is an exact fixed-\(A\) graphical theorem and a conditional law-level implication, not completeness.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A graphical replacement now specifies \(\widetilde S\), \(\widetilde G_0\), and \(\widetilde T\) explicitly, but this does not construct a law-level model. The exceptional-set argument is conditional on first supplying a nonempty open rational parameterization of equality-constrained shared-exogenous response-function models that satisfies the Markov direction, strict positivity, and positive denominators. Constructing that parameterization for every replacement and showing one determinant is nonzero for every \(m\)-connected query are both open. Moreover, exact equality on the fixed-\(A\) graphical fiber does not infer faithful two-mark witnesses, and neither result supplies a finite observable unknown-\(A\) rule list or a common exterior completion. No separation margin or finite-sample test theorem is present, so simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs are outside the proved scope.
body.honest_scope: Proved content is an exact fixed-selection-ancestry endpoint characterization on a purely structural Dai graphical fiber, \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\), obtained by necessity and explicit empty-graph or simple signature-monotone-path constructions. At law level the proved relation is \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{faith}}\subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}\), with equality automatic for singleton \(\mathcal G_A\) and conditional on nonempty realization fibers for two marks. The finite polynomial exceptional-set argument is valid only for a supplied nonempty open rational shared-response parameterization satisfying the Markov direction and atomic nontriviality. The construction of that parameterization, the atomic certificates, opposing faithful two-mark witnesses, a fixed observable unknown-\(A\) extension calculus, unconditional canonical SI-PAG equality, and simultaneous finite-sample confidence guarantees remain open. If a fixed polynomial-time rule list satisfying the two open antecedents is later supplied, its closure has at most \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates and equals the canonical target by a conditional implication. The scope excludes latent common causes among measured variables, post-treatment or regime-specific selection, and a global basal-DAG enumerator as the headline method.
